meta.title: Forest Futures
meta.subtitle: A strategic foresight game for forest leaders
meta.credits: Evolved from “IMPACT: a foresight game – forestry edition” (2019) by the Strategic Foresight Group — David N. Bengston and Lynne M. Westphal (USDA Forest Service, Northern Research Station) and Michael J. Dockry and Jason S. Crabtree (University of Minnesota) — itself an adaptation of IMPACT, designed by Idea Couture in collaboration with Policy Horizons Canada.
meta.notice: Signals are drawn from real-world sources; their effects in the game are speculative and meant to provoke discussion, not to predict. This is an independent tool, not an official product of USDA or any agency.

domains.name: Fire & Fuels
domains.description: Wildfire risk and behavior, fuels, prescribed and cultural fire, suppression capacity, smoke.
domains.examples: Fuels treatments, fire seasons, burn windows, suppression costs

domains.name: Forest Health
domains.description: Biodiversity, insects and disease, invasive species, drought stress, reforestation and adaptation.
domains.examples: Bark beetles, seed supply, mortality, restoration

domains.name: Water & Watersheds
domains.description: Source water, snowpack, streams, floods, post-fire watersheds and aquatic habitat.
domains.examples: Municipal supply, snow drought, debris flows, dam removal

domains.name: Climate & Carbon
domains.description: Forest carbon storage, carbon markets, emissions, bioenergy and climate policy.

domains.name: Wood Economy
domains.description: Timber, mills, mass timber, biomass, non-timber forest products and trade.
domains.examples: Mill capacity, lumber prices, tariffs, new wood materials

domains.name: Communities & the WUI
domains.description: Rural economies, growth in the wildland–urban interface, housing, insurance, equity and community health.
domains.examples: Home hardening, insurance retreat, rural jobs, smoke exposure

domains.name: Recreation & Public Connection
domains.description: Outdoor recreation, access, visitation, wellness and public trust in land managers.
domains.examples: Visitor services, trail backlog, fees, nature and health

domains.name: Workforce & Capacity
domains.description: Agency and partner workforce, fire crews, contractors, skills, and science, data and technology capacity.
domains.examples: Staffing, hiring, retention, training, research capacity, AI tools

domains.name: Policy & Funding
domains.description: Budgets, authorities, legislation, litigation, agency structure and federal–state roles.

domains.name: Partnerships & Co-Stewardship
domains.description: Tribal co-stewardship, shared stewardship with states, Good Neighbor agreements, NGOs, and private and family forest owners.
domains.examples: Co-management agreements, cross-boundary projects, landowner programs

eras.name: Now
eras.description: Trends already in motion and decisions already made. High certainty, little time.

eras.name: Near
eras.description: Emerging changes that are plausible within a planning cycle or two.

eras.name: Far
eras.description: Weak signals and wildcards. Low certainty, high consequence.
